test.title: Mini-test · What future for the high street?

paragraphs.text: Shopping streets in many towns have lost shops to online retailers and out-of-town centres. Economist Ruth Coleman argues that the decline is permanent and that towns should stop trying to fill empty shops, turning the buildings into homes instead.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Retail consultant David Marsh disagrees. He believes shops can survive if they offer experiences that cannot be bought online, such as cooking classes in kitchen stores or repair services in bike shops. He points to a town in Yorkshire where empty units fell by half after owners were helped to run events.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Architect Nina Osei focuses on the street itself. She says that wider pavements, trees and places to sit encourage people to stay longer, and that visitors who stay longer spend more. However, she warns that such improvements take years to pay off.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: The Local Traders’ Association, which represents small businesses, argues that high business rates are the main problem and has asked the government to reduce them for independent shops. Coleman replies that lower rates would only delay the closure of shops that customers no longer need.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Historian Samuel Price reminds planners that high streets have always changed. A century ago, he notes, many were dominated by banks and butchers; today’s cafés and hairdressers are simply the latest stage. He believes local people should decide what their town centre becomes.
paragraphs.label: E

document.title: Mini-test · What future for the high street?

items.quote: turning the buildings into homes instead
items.prompt: suggests converting empty shops into places to live

explanation.en: Coleman: instead of filling shops, “turning the buildings into homes” → A.
explanation.kk: Коулман: жалдаушы іздеудің орнына «turning the buildings into homes» → A.
explanation.ru: Коулман: вместо поиска арендаторов — «turning the buildings into homes» → A.

items.quote: He points to a town in Yorkshire where empty units fell by half
items.prompt: gives an example of a town where the number of empty shops fell

explanation.en: Marsh gives the example of a town in Yorkshire where empty units “fell by half” → B.
explanation.kk: Марш мысал келтіреді: бос үй-жайлар «fell by half» болған Йоркширдегі қала → B.
explanation.ru: Марш приводит пример: город в Йоркшире, где пустые помещения «fell by half» → B.

items.quote: such improvements take years to pay off
items.prompt: warns that improvements to the street will not bring quick benefits

explanation.en: Osei warns that “such improvements take years to pay off” → C. “Not … quick” = “take years”.
explanation.kk: Осей ескертеді: «such improvements take years to pay off» → C. «Not … quick» = «take years».
explanation.ru: Осей предупреждает: «such improvements take years to pay off» → C. «Not … quick» = «take years».

items.quote: has asked the government to reduce them for independent shops
items.prompt: wants a tax on businesses to be lowered

explanation.en: The traders’ association asks for lower “business rates” → D. Coleman, in the same paragraph, opposes this.
explanation.kk: Саудагерлер қауымдастығы «business rates» азайтуды сұрайды → D. Сол абзацта Коулман, керісінше, бұған қарсы.
explanation.ru: Ассоциация торговцев просит снизить «business rates» → D. Коулман в том же абзаце, наоборот, против этого.

items.quote: today’s cafés and hairdressers are simply the latest stage
items.prompt: places recent changes in a long historical context

explanation.en: Price compares with a century ago: cafés and hairdressers are “simply the latest stage” → E.
explanation.kk: Прайс ғасыр бұрынғымен салыстырады: кафе мен шаштараз — «simply the latest stage» → E.
explanation.ru: Прайс сравнивает с тем, что было век назад: кафе и парикмахерские — «simply the latest stage» → E.

items.quote: shops can survive if they offer experiences that cannot be bought online
items.prompt: believes shoppers need reasons to visit that the internet cannot offer
keywords: experiences that cannot be bought online

explanation.en: Marsh: shops survive by offering “experiences that cannot be bought online” → B. B is used twice — there is an NB.
explanation.kk: Марш: дүкендер «experiences that cannot be bought online» ұсынса, аман қалады → B. B екінші рет — NB бар.
explanation.ru: Марш: магазины выживут, если предложат «experiences that cannot be bought online» → B. B второй раз — есть NB.

items.quote: Coleman replies that lower rates would only delay the closure of shops that customers no longer need
items.prompt: argues that reducing a cost will not save shops in the long run

explanation.en: Coleman’s reply in paragraph D: “lower rates would only delay the closure” → A. The paragraph is about the association (D), but the view is Coleman’s.
explanation.kk: D абзацындағы Коулманның жауабы: «lower rates would only delay the closure» → A. Абзац қауымдастық (D) туралы, бірақ бұл пікір Коулманікі.
explanation.ru: Ответ Коулман в абзаце D: «lower rates would only delay the closure» → A. Этот абзац об ассоциации (D), но мнение принадлежит Коулман.

items.quote: visitors who stay longer spend more
items.prompt: links the time visitors spend in a town to how much they spend

explanation.en: Architect Osei links time and spending: “visitors who stay longer spend more”. Those who stay longer buy more → C.
explanation.kk: Сәулетші Осей уақыт пен шығынды байланыстырады: «visitors who stay longer spend more». Ұзақ қалған көбірек сатып алады → C.
explanation.ru: Архитектор Осей связывает время и траты: «visitors who stay longer spend more». Кто дольше остаётся, тот больше покупает → C.

items.quote: He believes local people should decide what their town centre becomes
items.prompt: thinks residents should shape the future of the town centre

explanation.en: Historian Price thinks residents should decide: “local people should decide what their town centre becomes”. “Shape the future” paraphrases “decide what … becomes” → E.
explanation.kk: Тарихшы Прайс тұрғындар шешуі керек деп санайды: «local people should decide what their town centre becomes». «Shape the future» — «decide what … becomes» дегеннің басқаша айтылымы → E.
explanation.ru: Историк Прайс считает, что решать должны жители: «local people should decide what their town centre becomes». «Shape the future» пересказывает «decide what … becomes» → E.

items.quote: The Local Traders’ Association, which represents small businesses
items.prompt: speaks on behalf of small business owners

explanation.en: The association “represents small businesses”, so it speaks for small business owners → D.
explanation.kk: Қауымдастық «represents small businesses» — шағын бизнес иелерінің атынан сөйлейді → D.
explanation.ru: Ассоциация «represents small businesses» — говорит от имени владельцев малого бизнеса → D.

groups.instruction: Questions 1–10. Look at the following statements and the list of people and organisations below. Match each statement with the correct person or organisation, A–E. NB You may use any letter more than once.
